reuse.why: All month-wide actions, including the new last-month-spending action, go through one shouldFillCategory and spendingToBudgetAmount, and setNMonthAvg reuses the sign helper; copyPreviousMonth keeps its own getBudgetData query that re-adds the group-notes join.

duplication.why: The three copied category queries, the income/hidden checks and the sign flips collapse into shared helpers; small leftovers are the FillCategory/BudgetData field overlap and the notes join written in both getBudgetData and getFillCategories.

placement.why: Eligibility and amount conversion live as private helpers in budget/actions.ts beside the actions, and the new method is registered in app.ts like its siblings.

scope.why: Edits serve the refactor and the four steps; release notes are added, and the includeHiddenCategories flag is threaded through each action as requested.

maintainability.why: A future change to eligibility (as steps 1, 3 and 4 show) lands in shouldFillCategory once; the requireGroup option makes the averages' group-join quirk explicit, though its name is somewhat opaque.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth, setZero, set3/6/12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending all call shouldFillCategory (directly or via getAverageFillCategories); amounts go through spendingToBudgetAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The only overlap (group notes join and field list in getBudgetData vs getFillCategories) is visible and small, not a reshaped copy of the rule.

abstraction_drift.where: shouldFillCategory takes requireGroup (the preserved averages-only group-exists quirk, a branch special to the average actions) and includeHidden (step 4's requested flag); the template and #fixed rules are added as plain rule checks inside it; no call site re-implements the decision.
